text:
maria: FYI opened a docs PR with a short playbook for GPU->CPU/quantized fallback handling in the model catalog. link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/1289 :eyes:

josh: skimmed. main ask: we need a clear compatibility matrix row for "aurora-xl -> aurora-lite (quantized)" and measured perf delta. can you add a bench table?

maria: yup planning to add a tiny table. provisional numbers are from raw bench runs: throughput -20%, p99 +12ms on small batches. i'll mark them as preliminary and attach the benchmark script.

toni: heads-up — we also need to update the SDK snippet to show `fallback_model` usage and mention tokenization caveats for quant variants.

liam: found one broken anchor in the catalog page: the GPU fallback section link points to `#gpu-fallbacks` but the header is `#gpu-fallback-playbook`. i'll open a tiny patch for that after the main PR merges.

devex-bot: CI status: docs/check-links passed, docs/markdown-lint failed on 2 files (line-length). 

maria: thanks bot. i'll fix the line-lengths, probably wrap the bench table and long notes.

josh: quick bench script so folks can reproduce (put in PR diff):
```bash
# run a 5-run latency profile for aurora-xl + aurora-lite fallback
python tools/bench_profile.py --model aurora-xl --fallback aurora-lite --seq 1024 --warm 10 --runs 5
```

toni: SDK snippet suggestion (inline in docs):
```python
from redwood import RedwoodClient
rc = RedwoodClient(api_key="$REDWOOD_KEY")
resp = rc.generate(model="aurora-xl", prompt="<prompt>", fallback_model="aurora-lite", max_tokens=256)
print(resp.text)
```
Add a short note: "fallback_model is attempted only on model errors or OOM; it does not change tokenization—ensure prompt/stop behavior is validated against the fallback model."

liam: also add a one-line link to the runtime compatibility matrix: https://docs.redwood.ai/model-catalog#compatibility-matrix (anchor currently works but double-check after my anchor fix).

maria: PR checklist for reviewers: add compatibility matrix row, attach bench CSVs, update SDK snippet, confirm link anchors, and ensure playbook has rollback steps for degraded quality (example text included). tagging reviewers: @josh, @toni, @liam. :pray:

josh: i'll run the recorded bench script after lunch and paste raw numbers here. will also sanity-check p50/p90/p99.

toni: will review the SDK snippet for wording and edge-case note about quantized tokenizer truncation.

liam: opened tiny PR for anchor rename: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/1290 — it's safe to merge anytime, will rebase if needed.

sre-bot: deploy-monitor: noticed a brief surge on aurora-xl cluster during evening tests, no errors, spike cleared. tagging in case the playbook text should mention transient capacity spikes.

maria: good catch — i'll add a short section: "operational note: transient capacity spikes may increase fallback rate; monitor p50/p99 and error_rate and consider autoscale/burst rules."

josh: small nit — in the compatibility matrix row please add a column "expected degradation" with a short summary (e.g., "~20% throughput, p99 +10–15ms (prelim)"). helps product and TOC reviewers.

maria: added that line and pushed to the PR. also included a short example migration checklist for customers switching variants.

toni: LGTM on content side, left two tiny wording suggestions in the PR comments around the tokenizer note.

liam: after anchor PR merges i'll do a quick doc search to fix any other stale links.

maria: thanks everyone — can we aim to merge main PR tomorrow morning during the docs merge window? i'll request the [release-note] label for the catalog change.

josh: can do, will drop final bench numbers here before EOD and then approve.

toni: i'll approve once wording tweaks are applied.

maria: wrapping up here — final checklist: squash commits, attach bench CSVs, add release-note label, re-run docs CI. i'll follow up once merged. :rocket:
